It extends the §5.11 / §5.12 / §5.35 DB-over-UI discipline to the actual side-effect target, and is the QA-facing generalization of BP-71 / BP-72.

**Why (DT-11 lesson):** checking only the UI-facing response (or a guard-path smoke) misses real bugs. DT-11 found two genuine production bugs only by exercising the ACTUAL charge/pay path and confirming DB + Stripe state, not the guard/error-response path:
- `renew-subscription` returned `INVALID_STATUS` on the shared active test-buyer (smoke "passed") yet its real renewal path was permanently blocked by the constant `sub_<row_id>` idempotency key — a renewal that would silently drop a user's subscription.
- `retry-failed-payment` returned `NO_FAILED_PAYMENT` (smoke "passed") yet could never pay an open invoice because it sent `paid_out_of_band: false` — a payment-retry button that could never succeed.

Rules:
1. **Side-effect verification is mandatory.** For any UI action with a backend/DB/third-party side effect, after the action completes (or fails), read the relevant DB rows and/or the Stripe/PayPal object state and confirm the side effect actually happened (or didn't, when a failure was expected) — never rely on the UI response alone.
2. **Real-activation verification is required, not just guard-path smoke checks**, whenever the function's main purpose is to move money or mutate financial state (subscriptions, payments, refunds, payouts). A guard-path probe (`INVALID_STATUS` / `NO_FAILED_PAYMENT` / `NO_OPEN_INVOICE` / `SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_ACTIVATED`) that returns the expected error does NOT prove the real path works — drive the actual charge/pay path on a fresh, isolated throwaway user (own Stripe customer + own payment method) and confirm the resulting object/row state (BP-71 / BP-72).
3. **This class of backend/DB/Stripe read-only verification is pre-approved** — read-only confirmation of DB rows and Stripe/PayPal object state does not require manual owner approval per instance (consistent with §5.14's "read-only SQL stays permitted" discipline). **Mutating test actions are NOT covered:** creating/cancelling real test trades, subscriptions, or refunds still follows the existing safe-fixture/disposable-user discipline — throwaway users where money movement is involved (see §7 personas, BP-70 cleanup, §5.36 fixture collision).
4. **Worked example (DT-11 pattern):** create a disposable/throwaway user (isolated from test-buyer/test-seller) → exercise the REAL path (not just the guard) → confirm BOTH the third-party (Stripe) object state AND the corresponding database row → then clean up the throwaway user (BP-70: delete child rows, `profiles` by `user_id`, then `admin.deleteUser`).
5. **Worked example (TRD Group A/B, 2026-08-28 — A02):** the UI showed "You saved $8.00 using SP! You have 38 SP left" on trade completion while the DB proved the SP-settlement trigger was missing (`final_sp_amount=0`, `seller_sp_earned=0`, `sp_released_at` NULL, 8 SP stuck reserved, no `sp_ledger` rows) — a P1 found only because the money state was read back from the DB (see §5.38 R11). A UI success screen is evidence the request completed, never evidence the financial state persisted.

### 5.38 Standing rules — TRD Group A/B run (2026-08-28) — consolidated playbook updates (R1–R16)

This subsection consolidates the 16 standing rules derived from the TRD Group A/B execution run — evidence source: `e2e-test-results/qa-trd-group-a-b-2026-08-28/decision-outcome-log.md` (667 tool executions; 9 PASS · 2 FAIL · 4 BLOCKED · 5 SKIPPED; P1 SP-settlement + P1/P2 Stripe idempotency findings). Where a rule restates an existing §5.x section, the earlier section remains canonical and this entry only adds the new evidence or the correction; where a rule corrects an earlier assumption, the earlier section has been updated in place (marked "Phase 13.43").

**R1 — Native modals are invisible to the accessibility tree — go straight to pixel-scan.** Any native alert/bottom-sheet (`Accept`/`Decline`/`Cancel` confirmations, the cancellation-reason sheet) returns an empty or near-empty element tree. Do not attempt to re-list or search the tree for these — immediately fall back to OCR/pixel-scan (§5.4). Know the app's palette so the first scan is correct: primary/confirm green `#5DBB8E`, destructive/danger red `#ff6b6b`, disabled pink `#ffb3b3` (plus the disabled-gray `#E8E8E8`). If a button's color/state is ambiguous, read the component source directly (e.g. `CancellationReasonModal.tsx`) rather than guessing — this run wrongly assumed a confirm button was green when it was red, costing extra scans. *Evidence: B04 (P6) cancel-reason sheet; A01/A02 (P3/P4) seller-accept OK.*

**R2 — Never tap by coordinate while the keyboard is up.** Reaffirms the existing §5.2 / §5.19 Rule 1 hard gate: send the keyboard-hide keystroke (`Cmd+K`) before ANY coordinate-based tap following text entry, then re-list for fresh coordinates. This run's ~60 `Cmd+K` calls are the cost of the gate; a device-level dismiss-keyboard affordance is the instrumentation fix (log §7 item 5). *Evidence: every phase (P2.1, P3.1, P4.4–4.5…).*

**R3 — Default to select-all-and-retype (`Cmd+A`) for clearing text fields — do NOT attempt long-press-then-Select-All first.** Long-press "Select All" does not work reliably in this app (failed twice on the SP numeric field; and in the TRD C/D/E run it surfaced no edit menu at all, with `Cmd+A` the working fix). Go directly to the select-all keystroke (`Cmd+A`) + retype for ANY field-clear/retype need — skip the failed technique entirely rather than trying it once per field. Updates §5.10 / §5.13: `Cmd+A` is the standing default; long-press → Select All is only worth attempting on field types already proven to support it this build. *Evidence: P4.5 SP-field clearing (F6); TRD C/D/E P2 login-field repairs (Round 2, §5.39).*

**R4 — After any LogBox/Console-Error overlay appears, terminate and relaunch immediately.** Don't attempt to dismiss the scrim or tap through it (the §5.19 Phase-13.42 full-screen-scrim finding means taps are eaten everywhere). The app session persists across a relaunch, so this is faster and more reliable than fighting the overlay — especially for *stale replays* of a previously-seen error. Strengthens §5.19 Rule 6: bounded-dismiss attempts apply to a first-time overlay; a recognized stale replay skips dismissal entirely. *Evidence: P2.9–2.10 (A01 Accept blocked by replayed idempotency error), P7.5 (freed-slot offer blocked by replayed cap error) — F1/F5.*

**R5 — Screenshot/view-image tools return a URI, not readable pixels.** Never attempt to "view" a screenshot directly for verification (`view_image` returned only a resource URI — 3 wasted calls, log §3). Route all visual checks through the OCR/pixel-scan `qa:*` helpers (§5.23) from the start. *Evidence: §3 tool inventory.*

**R6 — Search for deep-link routes during initial recon, not mid-run.** Deep links (`p2pkidsmarketplace://listing/<id>` → ItemDetail, `p2pkidsmarketplace://qa-logout`) are the standard way to reach fixtures that aren't reachable through normal in-app navigation (off-node/NULL-node items, persona switches). Find and note them in the first pass before starting case execution. Extends §5.16 (logout deep link) to all deep links. *Evidence: P1.3 (deep-link map found in recon) — the run's standard navigation tool.*

**R7 — Schema-first on any SQL column error.** If a query fails on a column name, inspect the actual schema before retrying — never guess a second column name. One retry per schema surprise, not a cascade. Reaffirms §5.34. *Evidence: P1.2 (`display_name`→`name`, `item_id`→`listing_id`), one retry each.*

**R8 — Trust the master tracker over inline guide annotations.** Any "passed"/informal annotation inside a canonical test-guide file that isn't reflected in the master coverage tracker (`TEST-COVERAGE-INVENTORY.md`) must be treated as unverified and re-run fresh. Confirm the tracker's actual state before trusting any in-document shortcut. *Evidence: P0.2 — all 20 cases were NEVER RUN despite inline annotations.*

**R9 — Batch DB verification instead of verifying after every single action.** When multiple similar actions are queued (e.g., filling multiple pending offers toward a cap), perform all the actions first, then verify the resulting state with one SQL query, rather than round-tripping to the DB after each individual action. Complements §5.27 (that rule covers a single simultaneous-evidence assertion; this covers a batch of actions). *Evidence: P7.1 — 3 offers submitted, verified in one query.*

**R10 — Check for reusable existing fixtures/state before building new state.** Before creating new test data for a case, check whether existing data already satisfies the precondition (e.g., an existing conversation on an already-cancelled trade). This run closed one case almost for free this way. Extends §5.33 (repurpose incidental state) to deliberate pre-checking. *Evidence: P9 — B08 reused the existing conversation on cancelled `c3d0146f`.*

**R11 — Always verify money/SP state via the database, never trust the UI success message alone.** A UI success screen proves the request completed, not that the backend correctly persisted the financial/points state. Every case with a financial or SP side effect must close the loop with a direct DB check before recording PASS. This is the QA-side confirmation of §5.37 (side-effect verification; read-only DB/Stripe checks pre-approved) — not a separate requirement. *Evidence: P4.8–4.10 — A02 UI said "You saved $8 / 38 SP" while the DB proved SP settlement was broken (P1).*

**R12 — Confirm root causes by reading actual source before recording a finding.** Every credible finding this run (idempotency-key construction, missing trigger, dead code, SP-only counter logic) was confirmed by reading the actual Edge Function, migration, trigger definition, or screen component — not inferred from a single observed symptom. Do this before writing up any bug finding. Complements §5.15 (stale-observation check), §5.25 (source-proven-impossible paths), §6.1 (two-source corroboration). *Evidence: P2.6 (idempotency key), P4.10 (missing trigger), P5.6 (dead code), P7.7 (SP-only counter).*

**R13 — Every BLOCKED/SKIPPED verdict must carry an explicit, evidence-backed reason.** Categorize precisely: missing fixture (B05e — `test-seller-3` does not exist), platform-level validation prevents the scenario (B06 — **now testable via the Dev Task 25 `card_decline` session-local QA toggle: arm `p2pkidsmarketplace://qa-dev-toggle?key=card_decline&value=hold_decline`, submit a normal valid card, and the hold-creation step returns STRIPE_HOLD_FAILED**), config-fetch-failure (B05i — **now testable via the Dev Task 25 `config_fetch_failure` toggle: arm `p2pkidsmarketplace://qa-dev-toggle?key=config_fetch_failure&value=fetch_failure` to reproduce the "Offer limit configuration is unavailable" rejection without a shared-staging admin_config mutation**), etc. Never leave an ambiguous or unexplained skip. *Evidence: P10 — 4 BLOCKED / 5 SKIPPED, each with an explicit reason.* **2026-08-31 correction** — "admin-portal-scope" is REMOVED as a valid category (standing rule, see `/memories/repo/qa-test-agent.md`): admin-dependent test cases are NEVER out of scope by default — a case needing the admin portal is the instruction to use it for real in the same session; a genuine admin blocker (portal unavailable, credentials issue) is BLOCKED with a stated reason, never labeled "admin-scope".

**R14 — For ANY timer-dependent RPC/processor, use the documented fast-clock approach and re-run once on a `0`/empty result before concluding failure.** Use the approved fast-clock (`UPDATE trades SET offer_expires_at = now() + interval '5 seconds'` + `rpc_process_expired_offers`; or `UPDATE trades SET auto_complete_at = now() + interval '5 seconds'` + `rpc_process_auto_complete`) instead of waiting out a timer. When the first RPC returns a `0`/empty result, re-check after a brief pause rather than immediately recording a failure — a zero first poll is very likely a race against the fast-clock window, not a real failure. *Evidence: P7.4 (B05d) — first run returned 0 (raced the 5s), rerun processed 1; TRD C/D/E P3 (D01 auto-complete) — `auto_completed_count:0` then `1` on re-run (Round 2, §5.39).*

**R15 — Avoid re-offering on a listing where the same buyer has a prior trade, until the idempotency-key fix (Task 18) lands.** Deterministic idempotency keys (`pi_offer_<buyer>_<item>_<hash(params)>`) collide when a buyer re-offers on a listing with params identical to a prior trade → Stripe 409. Prefer fresh listings with no prior buyer history for each new offer-submission test case, to avoid hitting the known collision and wasting a cycle on an already-understood bug. Distinct from §5.36 (which covers *concurrent* runs colliding on the same fixture); this rule covers *historical* prior trades on the same listing. *Evidence: P2.5–2.8 (A01 on `83c8823b` — the #1 bottleneck, F1).*

**R16 — Maintain a running friction/facts list in session memory throughout a run, not just at the end.** Capture discovered environment quirks (keyboard technique, native-modal colors, the `Cmd+A` trick, screenshot-tool limitation, seller-fee flag) as they're found, so later phases in the same run — and future sessions — start from known facts instead of rediscovering them. Formalizes §9's running list as a session-memory artifact written continuously during the run. *Evidence: P11.2 (session-memory update) — pattern P10.*

### 5.39 Standing rules — TRD Group C/D/E run (2026-08-28) — Round 2 consolidated playbook updates (R17–R22 + merges into R3/R14)

This subsection consolidates the second round of standing rules derived from the TRD Group C/D/E (+ B02/B03/B05c carryover) execution run — evidence source: `e2e-test-results/qa-trd-b-c-d-e-2026-08-28/decision-outcome-log.md` (24 cases; 19 PASS · 0 FAIL · 5 BLOCKED · 0 SKIPPED; P1/P2 auto-complete payout gap, P2 Report-Problem occlusion, P2 TradeDispute-unreachable, P2 category-driven SP cap findings). It builds on Round 1 (§5.38, R1–R16, from the Group A/B run): **two Round 2 items refined existing rules and were MERGED in place rather than duplicated — item 4 (any timer RPC, re-run on `0`) → R14; item 7 (`Cmd+A` default for field clears) → R3.** The six remaining items are new and appear as R17–R22 below. The §5.38 policy applies here too: where a rule restates an existing §5.x section, the earlier section remains canonical and this entry only adds the new evidence or the correction.

**R17 — Screenshot/OCR is the source of truth the instant AX coordinates look suspicious: overlapping the floating tab pill, or reporting a y-coordinate greater than the screen height.** Don't burn tap attempts on coordinates the AX reports if either condition is true — go straight to OCR/screenshot verification first. The floating `PersistentTabBar` pill (absolute, floats over content) covers bottom-anchored buttons while the AX tree reports their logical coordinates without z-order; and AX reports logical/content coordinates for below-fold rows even when they render off-screen (y > screen height = not tappable). This run's silent no-op taps (checkout `send-offer-button` at y=1064 on a 956pt screen; Report Problem occluded by the pill with no scroll path) were all preventable by OCR-first. Extends §5.1/§5.2 (below-fold logical coords) and §5.9 (screenshot is the source of truth). *Evidence: P4/E01 (report-problem-button occlusion), P7 (basket CTA + checkout Send Offer under the pill / off-screen).*

**R18 — Pre-read the relevant source file before touching any screen/flow not yet mapped this session.** Source reads (not UI exploration) are consistently the fastest way to resolve: reachability questions (is this route ever navigated to? — `TradeDispute` is registered but no screen calls `navigate('TradeDispute')` and no deep link maps it → E07–E10 BLOCKED), threshold values (color/cap/timing logic — `countdown.ts` pill thresholds, `calculateCategorySP` caps), and root causes of any "UI says X, DB says Y" discrepancy (the auto-complete payout gap was proven by reading `rpc_process_auto_complete` + `fn_queue_payout_on_complete`). Treat a grep-first approach as the default, not a fallback. Reinforces §4 flow-registry/source pre-read (Phase 18/22) and R12 (confirm by source before recording a finding); this entry adds the "resolve reachability/thresholds upfront" bias. *Evidence: P3 (payout-gap root-cause chain), P4 (TradeDispute reachability), P5 (pill thresholds).*

**R19 — Batch all offers/logins by persona, and seed precondition state via direct SQL insert (then delete afterward) rather than driving it through the UI when the case under test isn't the precondition itself.** Persona login/switch is consistently the most expensive recurring operation (7 persona logins this run, each ~3–6 extra taps + 1–2 `Cmd+A` repairs); minimize the count of switches per run, and only drive through the real UI the specific flow being tested. Precondition offers/state (D03's four pending offers at staggered ages, B05c's two pending offers) were seeded directly via SQL and deleted afterward — cheaper and avoids re-hitting saved-card flakiness. Extends §5.26 (batch by persona) and R9 (batch DB verification); complements §5.33 (repurpose incidental state) and R10 (reuse existing state before building new). *Evidence: P5 (D03 seeding), P7 (B05c seeding), §4.3 (login tax).*

**R20 — For color/design-system verification on near-white or pastel UI elements, scan border and fill colors, not background — backgrounds quantize to white and produce false negatives in a low-color-count histogram. Locate the exact element band via thin-strip OCR first, then run the color scan on that band.** Near-white pill backgrounds (#EFF6FF / #FFFBEB / #FEF2F2 / #F8FAFC) merged to white in the 12-color quantizer; the D03 pill band was located by thin-strip OCR (y 1110–1260), then the border + green progress-fill colors were scanned deterministically. Tooling note: `qa:badge-scan` token keys use `name=…`, not a bare color name (one retry this run). Complements R1 (native-modal palette) and §6.4 (design-system compliance); the strip-OCR-then-band-scan sequence is the new deterministic technique. *Evidence: P5 (D03 pill histograms).*

**R21 — When a UI path is source-proven unreachable (no navigation call, no deep link, physically occluded with no scroll path), stop investigating immediately and record BLOCKED with the specific evidence (grep result, occlusion measurement, etc.). If the blocked case is actually about verifying a *state* rather than a UI interaction, substitute a DB-level setup for that state and continue testing the downstream behavior, documenting the substitution explicitly.** E01 (Report Problem occluded by the pill with no scroll path) and E07–E10 (`TradeDispute` unreachable — no `navigate('TradeDispute')`, no deep link) were BLOCKED with evidence; the dispute *state* was then set via DB (mirroring `open-dispute/index.ts`'s exact columns) so D02/E02/E03/E04 could verify the downstream dispute-state behaviors (auto-complete blocked, dispute banners, button hiding). Reinforces §5.25 (fail fast when source proves a path impossible) and R13 (BLOCKED carries explicit reason) — the state-substitution continuation is the new step. *Evidence: P4 (E-series).*

**R22 — Before tapping any button, confirm it is within the visible viewport (y-coordinate less than the screen height) and not covered by the floating tab pill. If either is uncertain, re-list and OCR before tapping, rather than tapping speculatively.** Generalizes the below-fold check beyond the keyboard-up case (§5.2) to every tap: AX content coordinates ≠ rendered viewport, and the pill overlaps bottom CTAs without z-order in the tree. This is the pre-tap gate that prevents the R17 no-op-tap class — R17 is the detection signal, this is the confirmation step. *Evidence: P1/P7 (Send Offer at y=1064, two silent no-op taps).*

### 5.40 Standing rules — Dev Task 51 QA-toolkit round 2 (2026-08-29) — decision-log-driven playbook updates (R23–R28)

This subsection encodes the QA Task 5 decision-and-outcome log into standing rules so future runs adopt them proactively rather than relearning them. It also introduces the Dev Task 51 tooling that removes the friction the log measured (offer-fixture resets, one-call persona login, EF repro harness). Each rule names the exact tool/command where one exists.

**R23 — Read the backend/EF error before concluding a UI failure is an app bug.** The same generic UI failure message (e.g. "Couldn't send offer") can hide very different backend causes: `NO_PAYMENT_METHOD` (fixture missing saved card — fix via `npm run qa:ensure-cards`), `MAX_PENDING_OFFERS` (stale pending slots — fix via `npm run qa:reset-offer-fixtures`), `TRADE_INSERT_ERROR` (real DB/contract bug). Use the checked-in repro harness `npm run qa:ef-repro -- --persona <name> --ef create-trade-offer --items <id>` to invoke the EF directly with the persona's real JWT + saved card and read the RAW structured error before touching app code. Extends §5.15 (stale-observation) and §6.1; the EF-response read is the new first step. *Evidence: QA Task 5 K10/K04 diagnosis cost.*

**R24 — Close every money/SP/state assertion with a DB read-back — a UI success toast is not proof.** A green toast/success screen only proves the UI rendered; it does not prove the ledger/trade/wallet row was written correctly. For any money/SP/payout/state case, verify the actual DB rows (trades status, sp_ledger entries, subscription status, payout columns) directly after the UI assertion — this exact pattern is what caught the P1 payout-zeroing and P2 tax-ledger bugs in QA Task 5. Read-only DB verification is pre-approved (see §5.37a); there is no need to ask per instance. Reinforces §5.37 (side-effect verification is mandatory). *Evidence: QA Task 5 P1/P2.*

**R25 — Re-read the persona's `fee_state` / subscription state and the LIVE admin config before any money-related case — guide numbers go stale; the DB/config is the authoritative source.** The manual guide's example numbers (fee amounts, SP values, caps) age out of sync with staging; before asserting any money figure, read the persona's current subscription/fee state and the relevant `admin_config` keys (via read-only SQL) and compare against what the UI actually shows — never assert a hardcoded guide number as if it were current. Extends R12 (confirm by source before recording a finding). *Evidence: QA Task 5 stale-guide-number findings.*

**R26 — Verify bundle/offer fixtures (active-trade status, pending-slot counts) BEFORE assembling a new case, not after a failure.** A case that needs N pending offers or a clean cart should START from a verified state: run `npm run qa:reset-offer-fixtures` at the start of any session touching offers/bundles, and check the target persona's pending-slot count + cart before driving the case. The cost of a mid-run `MAX_PENDING_OFFERS`/already-in-active-trade collision (3+ diagnosis-and-cleanup cycles in the last run) is always higher than a 10-second pre-check. Extends §5.36 (fixture collision) and R19 (seed preconditions directly). *Evidence: QA Task 5 stale-fixture cost driver.*

**R27 — Prefer `data-testid` / AX-name-based taps over raw coordinates whenever occlusion is plausible.** Raw coordinate taps are the failure class behind the QA Task 5 alert-dismissal cost; the app now exposes deterministic AX identifiers for confirmations (e.g. `offer-accepted-ok-button`, `bundle-accepted-ok-button`, `offer-declined-ok-button`, `global-alert-button-<n>`) via the branded `GlobalAlertProvider` (Dev Task 51 item 4). When a native-looking alert appears, re-list the AX tree and tap by name/testID — do not guess coordinates. Complements R17/R22 (OCR/viewport discipline) with an identifier-first bias.

**R28 — Config toggles used for testing must be scoped AND their revert verified at cleanup, not just changed.** Any `admin_config` write made for a case (per §5.37a discipline) must be: (1) scoped to the exact test value, (2) reverted to the pre-run value after the case, and (3) the revert VERIFIED by a read-back `SELECT value FROM admin_config WHERE key=...` (and `updated_by` recorded) — a changed-and-forgotten toggle silently corrupts every downstream run. Same discipline for session-local QA toggles: disarm via the `qa-dev-toggle` deep link and confirm the disarmed value. Extends §5.37a. *Evidence: QA Task 5 config-leftover findings.*

### 5.41 Standing rules — Simulator/Device Busy Check (2026-08-29) — shared-resource exclusivity (R29)

This subsection adds the standing rule for coordinating access to the shared QA resources: the iOS Simulator instance (target UDID) and, when it is the shared resource, the admin-portal browser session / staging Supabase project. Dev Task work (48, 51, 52) and QA Task work now routinely run against the same simulator and the same staging project, sometimes back-to-back or overlapping. Two agents driving the same simulator concurrently would interleave taps, corrupt login/persona state, and produce false verdicts (a QA read of a screen state a dev agent's action just changed, or vice versa) — a real risk at the current session cadence, not a hypothetical one.

**R29 — Check the target simulator/browser session for an in-flight agent task BEFORE starting; if busy, wait and poll — never interleave.** Before any simulator/emulator interaction (or attaching to the shared admin-portal browser session, if that is the shared resource):

1. **Check for an in-flight session marker** — look for a shared "session in progress" signal tied to an active agent task: a running `xcrun simctl` session/process, an active `run-suite.sh` / Maestro orchestrator process, an `e2e-test-results/<run>/` directory still being written to, a recently-active dev/QA task in the local session store, or a live logged-in admin session on `:3001` mid-edit when the browser session is the shared resource.
2. **Check booted-simulator/process state** — run `xcrun simctl list devices booted` plus a `ps` scan for agent-driven processes on the same UDID (`expo run:ios`, `maestro`, `run-suite.sh`, Playwright) before launching/attaching to the app.
3. **If busy: wait and poll** rather than force-attaching or launching a second instance that could collide on the same UDID. Do not interleave actions on a device/session another task is driving — a verdict read from a screen another agent's action just changed is a false verdict.
4. **Applies symmetrically** — a QA agent also avoids starting while a Dev Task is mid-flight against the same simulator/staging environment, and the same holds in the reciprocal direction (a Dev Task should not start while a QA run holds the device). If dispatched mid-flight against a held device, wait for the holder to finish; do not force through.
5. **Instrumentation gap — fold into the next QA toolkit round:** the environment currently has NO first-class "another task is using this simulator" detector. The proposed mechanism is a lightweight lock file the agent writes on start and removes on finish (e.g. a per-UDID marker recording agent id, start time, and UDID, under a shared location such as `e2e-test-results/`), so future runs can check presence + age before launching instead of inferring busy-ness from process/session heuristics. Until it lands, use the §R29.1–2 heuristics above and treat "can't rule out another agent on this UDID" as busy. *Context: QA standing-rule addition 2026-08-29 — Dev Task 48/51/52 + QA Task work share the same iOS Simulator instance and staging Supabase project.*

### 5.42 Standing rules — QA Task 8 cumulative-regression efficiency (2026-08-30) — AX-first modal handling, gated checkboxes, tab-bar occlusion (R30–R32)

This subsection encodes three efficiency rules from the QA Task 8 cumulative regression run (DT-56a/56b/57/58) — evidence source: `e2e-test-results/qa-task8-cumulative-regression-2026-08-30/report.md`. All three fix the same cost pattern: the run spent 10–15 OCR band-scans + pixel color-inspections on three modal interactions that each resolve in 3–4 calls when the AX tree is trusted first and two geometry traps (a gated acknowledgment checkbox, the bottom tab-bar band) are known up front.

**R30 — Acknowledgment-gated modal fast path (checkbox → disabled primary).** Signal: a modal renders its primary button in the DISABLED state (pastel — `#ABDAC4` for the `#5DBB8E` primary at 0.5 opacity, or `#FFE7E7` for the `#FF6B6B` destructive at 0.5 opacity) with an "I have read and understand this disclaimer" row directly above it. Do NOT pixel-hunt for the checkbox: it is exposed in the AX tree as `disclaimer-modal-checkbox` at a fixed geometry (`x16 y812 w408 h24`, full-width row, center `(220, 824)`). Fast path is exactly: (1) grep the tree for `disclaimer-modal-checkbox` and read its `value`; (2) tap the **row center** `(220, 824)` — NOT the box corner (~x28) and NOT the y≈840–853 band (that band is the Cancel/Accept row and misses the toggle); (3) re-list and assert `value:"checked"`; (4) tap `disclaimer-modal-accept-button` at its tree center `(325, 878)`. *Evidence: QA Task 8 Flow 2 — the checkbox was found only after band-OCR + color-scan confirmed the button was disabled because `accepted=false`; the AX-first path resolves it in 2 taps + 1 verify.*

**R31 — Never tap a CTA whose y-center is in the bottom tab-bar band (y≈848–904).** On tabbed screens, action buttons pinned at the bottom of a scrollable screen report bounds that overlap the tab bar (e.g. `cancel-trade-button` at `y=854` overlaps the bar at y≈848–892). Tapping the button's reported center can land on a tab — in QA Task 8, tapping the cancel button's center `(220, 878)` hit the **Sell** tab (x192–248) and navigated away (one full re-open + scroll cycle wasted). Fast path: BEFORE tapping, if a button's reported y-center is ≥ ~840, swipe the scrollable content **up** so the button's reported y-center drops below ~790, re-list to confirm it no longer overlaps the tab-bar band, THEN tap. If the tree reports a y-center < 840 the button is safe. Do not attempt a "partial-overlap" tap inside the tab-bar band.

**R32 — CancellationReasonModal: re-list the tree before any OCR; tap reason-row centers; verify the confirm button's enabled fill.** On open the modal's tree may be collapsed (only the clock). Re-list once — the reason rows populate on the second listing as `cancellation-reason-<id>` Buttons with known geometry (this run: `found_elsewhere` ~y238, `changed_mind` ~y308, `other` ~y378; each row is ~61px tall **including its subtitle**, so tap the row center e.g. `(220, 338)` for Changed mind — a tap at ~y305 lands between rows and selects nothing). The confirm `cancel-trade-confirm-button` is at `(224, 896)` → center `(324, 917)`, and is DISABLED (pastel `#FFE7E7`) until a reason is selected; when enabled it is solid red `#FF6B6B`. Fast path: select the reason row center from the tree → verify the confirm button's fill is `#FF6B6B` (if still pastel, the reason didn't register — re-tap the row, don't re-scan pixels) → tap the confirm center. Only if the second listing is still empty fall back to band-OCR (reason bands ~y270 / ~y336 / ~y390; confirm at ~y905). *Evidence: QA Task 8 Flow 2 — the first run band-scanned the modal and tapped at y≈305 (gap) and y≈878 (above the confirm), adding ~8 calls before the tree-exposed coordinates were used.*

**Meta-rule — AX-tree-first for every modal (extends §5.1 / R27):** before ANY OCR band-scan, pixel color inspection, or coordinate guess inside a modal, list the AX tree and re-list once — modals populate on the second listing. Tree coordinates are authoritative for taps; OCR/pixel-scan is the fallback ONLY when the second listing is still empty. The three rules above are concrete instances of this meta-rule.

### 5.43 Standing rules — QA Task 8 security-track money/SP verification discipline (2026-08-30) — R33–R36

This subsection encodes the four money-path verification standards from the QA Task 8 security-track run (Dev Tasks 54–59: cash portion, money-trust audit, grant lockdowns, RPC identity, tax checkout, grant sweep). They close the class of invariants a scripted DOM/AX suite cannot see.

**R33 — Scripted suites (Maestro/Detox/`run-suite.sh`) are a smoke layer only; money/SP invariants are closed by DB read-back, not by a green automated run.** An automated DOM/AX assertion run proves the UI rendered and the happy path executed; it cannot prove ledger/wallet/trade rows were written correctly or that grants are tight. For ANY money/SP/payout/grant assertion, the DB-read-back methodology (§5.37 / R11 / R24) is the standard and is NOT optional even when the automated suite passes. *Evidence: QA Task 8 — the security-track findings (dispute-resolve traceability, SP-adjustment attribution) were DB-side only; no AX assertion could have caught them.*

**R34 — A live-verification harness run more than once against the same staging DB must APPEND-MERGE its fixture ledger, not overwrite between runs.** Overwriting orphans the first run's cleanup artifacts (its rows stay around untracked, or its cleanup IDs point at replaced rows). Treat the ledger as append-only per run: new run appends, then cleanup removes the union of all runs' artifacts. Extends §5.33 (repurpose state) and BP-70 (cleanup discipline).

**R35 — Assert admin-actor attribution on every money-affecting admin action — `actor_id`/`admin_id`/`resolved_by` must be non-NULL, not just that the money moved.** QA Task 8 found dispute-resolve and SP-adjustment paths where the money/state changed correctly but the acting-admin traceability was NULL (lost attribution). When verifying an admin money action, read back the audit/actor columns and assert they are populated, in addition to the balance/state change. Complements BP-48 (settings writes must pass `p_admin_id`) and extends R24 (DB read-back) to the attribution columns.

**R36 — Read the applied tax/fee rate from the DB/config, never a fixed guide number, when writing verification assertions.** Rates are admin-configurable and guide numbers go stale. When computing the expected money figure, SELECT the live rate first and use it in the assertion so a changed config can't silently invalidate the verdict. Extends R25 (pre-case live-config re-read) to assertion time.

### 5.44 Standing rules — Legitimate `admin_config` write paths for QA fixtures (DEV-TASK-65, 2026-08-30) — R37

QA Task 7 N01 rediscovered (the hard way, via wasted calls) that writing `admin_config` through MCP SQL now correctly fails with `P0001 UNAUTHORIZED`. That is the DT-56a/DT-59 security lockdown working as intended (`admin_config` holds every money lever), NOT a bug. Do NOT rediscover it again — use the documented legitimate paths below. *Evidence: `e2e-test-results/qa-task7-expanded-lmn-retest-2026-08-30/decision-and-outcome-log.md` D2; grants verified live 2026-08-30 (`upsert_admin_config_setting` → authenticated+service_role; `secure_upsert_admin_config` → service_role only).*

**R37 — Use the `qa:admin-config-set` helper (or the admin-portal UI/API) for ANY QA fixture that needs to set an `admin_config` value. Never attempt a raw MCP-SQL write** (anon/no-role JWT → `P0001 UNAUTHORIZED` — the lockdown working). The three legitimate paths, fastest first:

1. **Helper script (preferred, no UI/no server):** from `p2p-kids-marketplace/`:
   - `npm run qa:admin-config-set -- set --key <k> --value <v> [--category <cat>] [--data-type <t>] [--is-active true|false] [--is-secret true|false] [--admin-id <uuid>] [--dry-run]` — calls `public.upsert_admin_config_setting` (the exact shared BP-48 write RPC the admin settings pages + `/config` API use) authenticated with `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` from `.env`/`.env.staging` (the same credential the admin portal's server-side API routes use). The RPC's own guard (`current_setting('role')='service_role'` OR `admin_has_role(auth.uid())`) still applies — nothing is bypassed. The script auto-reads the row back after `set`; `get --key <k>` and `list [--category <cat>]` read current values. Defaults: `category=feature_flags`, `data-type=string`, `is-active=true`, `is-secret=false`, `admin-id=null` (null preserves the previous `updated_by` editor, per DT-59).
   - Verified live 2026-08-30: set `cart_min_value_cents` 0→7777→0 with DB read-back matching on both writes.
2. **Admin portal settings-page UI (browser, admin JWT):** what QA Task 7 N01 ended up using (e.g. `/settings/cart`). Slow but fully legitimate; the same RPC runs with `auth.uid()` = the signed-in admin.
3. **Admin portal API (portal must be running on `:3001`):** `PATCH http://localhost:3001/api/admin/config` with header `x-admin-secret: <ADMIN_UI_SECRET>` and body `{"key":"<k>","value":"<v>","user_id":null}` → server-side service_role → `secure_upsert_admin_config` (key/value only; preserves existing category; always `is_active=true`; auto-pauses listings when raising `min_listing_price`).

**R37 notes —** `qa:admin-config-set` NEVER re-grants/weakens anything; if it ever errors `P0001 UNAUTHORIZED`, the credential in `.env`/`.env.staging` is wrong or missing — fix the env, don't hunt for a bypass. Always restore fixture config values after the case (same zero-residue discipline as §5.37/D6) and record the touched keys + restored values in `App State Left Behind`.

### 5.45 Standing rules — Accepted verdict class for VoiceOver swipe-gesture testing (DEV-TASK-65, 2026-08-30) — R38

Dev Task 62's AX-modal fix (item 5) was repeatedly marked PARTIAL because VoiceOver swipe-gesture interaction "isn't directly testable via the current mobile-mcp tooling." DEV-TASK-65 investigated option (a) — drive VoiceOver swipe gestures for real — and concluded it is infeasible with any available tool; the accepted convention is option (b), a named verdict class, so future runs classify consistently instead of rediscovering the limitation each time. *Evidence: `e2e-test-results/dev-task-65-qa-toolkit-r3-2026-08-30/` (investigation trace: plist enable attempts, Settings-UI attempt, gesture observations, tool-inventory enumeration).*

**R38 — For any AX/dialog/accessibility verification where the question is "does VoiceOver really work here?", classify with the accepted verdict class `AX-tree-exposure-verified, VoiceOver-swipe-interaction-not-directly-testable`** — NOT a rediscovered PARTIAL, and never a guess. The class is defined as:

- **Verified leg (must be done every time):** the element(s) ARE exposed in the iOS accessibility hierarchy — confirm via `mobile_list_elements_on_screen` (the AX tree is exactly what VoiceOver sees: BP-53-conformant testIDs/labels present with valid frames). This is the meaningful, assertable part of an AX fix.
- **Not-directly-testable leg (accepted limitation, no re-litigation):** the VoiceOver *gesture interaction model* (one-finger swipes to move the VoiceOver cursor, double-tap to activate, rotor rotation, spoken-utterance feedback) cannot be driven or observed by any available tool: mobile-mcp exposes only raw coordinate touches (no rotor / no focus-next / no activate-focused / no utterance capture), the AX tree does NOT report the VoiceOver cursor position or its speech, and the VoiceOver enable path itself is not reliably drivable on the shared iOS 26.1 sim (plist key didn't activate it; the Settings→Accessibility VoiceOver row is not AX-exposed). Maestro/WDA/`simctl` expose no VoiceOver APIs either. Concluding infeasible required no more than the bounded attempts above — do not burn calls re-attempting VoiceOver gesture driving.
- **How to label:** use the class name as the verdict in §8.1 item 3 AND in the §8.2 roll-up (count it under the accepted class, not PARTIAL/FAIL). In `Known Gaps / Not Tested`, state the untested leg explicitly: "VoiceOver swipe-interaction behavior (focus cursor movement, double-tap activation, rotor) was NOT directly driven — tooling cannot observe it; verdict covers AX-tree exposure only."
- **Do NOT:** mark such a case FAIL or PARTIAL purely because the VoiceOver swipe leg can't be driven; do NOT silently mark it PASS implying the gesture leg was tested. The class name says exactly what was and wasn't verified.

### 5.46 Standing rules — QA Task 11→13 process fixes (2026-08-31) — R39–R41

Process-discipline rules from the DT68→DT73 / QA11→QA13 arc. Unlike the interaction techniques in R30–R32 etc., these apply at **run-planning and scope-decision time**, not per-tap, so apply them before and between case execution. *Evidence: `e2e-test-results/qa-task12-close-2026-08-30/report.md` (A4 deferred table; P2 "Payment captured" copy finding), `e2e-test-results/qa-task13-dt71-dt72-verify-2026-08-31/report.md` (Section A/B copy re-verifies; C1 guide stale-copy flag). Companion Dev-side standing notes: `/memories/repo/agent-rule-updates-2026-08-31.md`.*

**R39 — When a copy/UI change lands, re-verify all cases whose expected-copy assertions it invalidates in the SAME or very next session** — do not only flag the guide entries as "stale" for a future round. Model behavior from QA Task 13: DT72's SP-limit phrasing and DT73's authorized-vs-charged copy stayed flagged AND got re-verified on-device in the same arc (T01/T03/T05/T06, S-group banner, A1 accept-alert "Payment authorized"). Make proactive re-verification the default, not an exception; a guide stale-copy flag (C1) is a finding, never a substitute for re-running the affected cases.

**R40 — When multiple deferred/owed cases are pending a user scope decision, require an explicit per-case list — never accept a general "these are deferred" note.** Present the batch with every TC-ID accounted for, and require the user's in-scope / out-of-scope / deferred-with-reason response to enumerate EVERY case; flag any mismatch back immediately rather than proceeding on an incomplete list. QA Task 12 exposed the gap: the user's 4 in-scope + 4 out-of-scope list did not cover all 9 previously-deferred cases (Q10 unaccounted for). A case is only "resolved" when the user's answer explicitly names it.

**R41 — Multi-account / aged-fixture cases (Q05/Q15/Q17/Q10 class) need DEDICATED fixture-building sessions — budget for them explicitly.** These consistently require assembling multi-account (second-party review on a profile; 3 distinct reporters for auto-hide) or time-aged (24h edit window, 30-day cooldown, 24h post-completion lock) fixtures that cannot be assembled opportunistically inside a broader batch. When these are back in scope, plan a dedicated fixture-building session and state it in the run plan — do not fold them into a general batch and mark deferred again.

### 5.47 Standing rules — QA Task 15 friction-analysis fixes (2026-08-31) — R-NEW-1..6 + codified facts

Zero-dev-cost rules derived from the QA Task 15 decision-and-outcome log — evidence source: `e2e-test-results/qa-task15-dt75-w-t-2026-08-31/decision-outcome-log.md` (~90 of ~250–300 calls were lost to avoidable friction: stuck-alert coordinate guessing, stale TradeList AX, admin 2-call deferrals, invisible SP inputs, schema-drift column guesses, empty-tree re-list loops, wrong-seller persona switches, undiscovered modal gating, deep-link dead ends, duplicate fixtures, fixture gaps). All six rules are **pure playbook/memory discipline — no dev work required — and apply from the very next QA session.** They sit alongside (not inside) the R1–R41 sequence; where a rule restates an existing §5.x section, the earlier section remains canonical and this entry adds the sharper trigger + the cheaper response. Companion dated consolidation in `/memories/repo/qa-test-agent.md` (2026-08-31 entry).

**R-NEW-1 — Relaunch-first on a blind AX tree (the single biggest fix).** If `mobile_list_elements_on_screen` returns only status-bar content (or is empty) **twice in a row**, do NOT coordinate-guess, do NOT OCR-crop-and-zoom, do NOT keep re-listing. Immediately `terminate` + `launch` the app (2 calls). If the tree is still blind after relaunch, stop and mark the case **BLOCKED** with the reason stated — do not keep trying. Two consecutive empty/status-bar-only lists are the "broken-screen-state" signal: a stuck modal/alert makes the toolset render only the status bar, and a relaunch clears it in 2 calls — this turns QA Task 15's worst 20-call stuck-"Offer Declined"-alert scenario into a 2-call fix. Deliberately distinct from §5.4's native-`Alert.alert` case (tree blanks while a real OS alert is genuinely up — OCR-first is correct there); R-NEW-1 applies when the tree is blind with no alert expected, after a failed dismiss, or when the blind tree persists across an action — when in doubt, one relaunch is cheaper than the guessing loop. *Evidence: QA Task 15 P4 — ~20 calls spent tapping/OCR-cropping a stuck GlobalAlert before a 2-call relaunch cleared it (F1/F6).*

**R-NEW-2 — Deep-link-first navigation.** Always attempt a deep link before multi-tap UI navigation; maintain a running cached list in session/repo memory of which deep links work and which are dead ends, so future sessions never rediscover the same dead end. Confirmed dead ends are cached and NOT retried (e.g., `p2pkidsmarketplace://trade/<id>` does NOT navigate — React Navigation linking config has no TradeDetail/TradeTimeline path, only the notification service parses `/trade/:id`; navigate via UI instead). Complements §5.16 (qa-logout) and R6 (map deep links in recon) — this adds the standing negative cache. *Evidence: QA Task 15 A4 — the `/trade/<id>` dead end cost ~4 calls before being abandoned (F9).*

**R-NEW-3 — Schema-consult before SQL.** Before writing any SQL query, check `/memories/repo/schema-cheat-sheet.md` for the table first. If the table/column isn't listed, run ONE `information_schema.columns` query and add the result to the cheat-sheet — one query up front is cheaper than 2–3 failed guesses. Reaffirms §5.34 / R7 (schema-first on a column error) by moving the check BEFORE the first query rather than after the first failure, and makes maintaining the cheat-sheet a standing duty, not an afterthought. *Evidence: QA Task 15 C5 — `sp_wallets.reserved_sp` (not `reserved_balance`), `cart_items.listing_id` (not `item_id`), `subscriptions.has_used_trial` (not `is_trial`) each cost 2–3 calls per wrong guess (F5).*

**R-NEW-4 — Seller-ownership check before persona switch.** When a test case depends on a specific seller owning a specific item, verify `items.seller_id` with ONE SQL query before logging in as a persona — don't assume which test-seller account owns an item. *Evidence: QA Task 15 C4 — Board Game Set is owned by test-seller-2, not test-seller; a wrong-seller login + re-switch + re-nav cost ~5 calls (F7).*

**R-NEW-5 — Batch admin-portal actions into one script.** In the admin portal, drive each page interaction as ONE `run_playwright_code` block that performs the clicks, reads the resulting state, and returns a JSON verdict — never one action per call. Prefer scripts that return inline JSON over large page snapshots + grep. Each `run_playwright_code` that mutates returns a deferred result needing a second call to fetch it — batching keeps that 2-call tax at once per page interaction instead of once per action, and JSON returns avoid 76KB-snapshot + resource-file greps. Complements §5.20 (embedded-browser DOM-level clicks; snapshot size) with the batch-assert + JSON-return discipline. *Evidence: QA Task 15 B2/W01–W12 — ~40+ calls for 12 admin cases, most from per-action 2-call deferred executions + huge snapshots + grep (F3).*

**R-NEW-6 — Fixture-feasibility check before starting a group.** Before starting a test group, run the 1–3 DB queries that prove the required fixtures actually exist (e.g., "are there any non-terminal bundles?" — `bool_or(status NOT IN ('completed','cancelled','payment_failed'))` over bundles; "how many Accept-SP items does this seller have?"; "is a 3-item same-seller Accept-SP bundle possible?"). Catching a fixture gap in one query up front beats discovering it by hunting the UI for several calls. Complements §5.25 (fail fast when source proves a path impossible) and R26 (verify fixtures before assembling) — this is the up-front DB feasibility gate. *Evidence: QA Task 15 B3 (W09/W10 — no non-terminal bundle existed → positive leg BLOCKED, negative leg PASS) and C1 (T06 — only 2 Accept-SP items existed, no 3-item scenario) (F11).*

### 5.47b Codified facts (no rule number — standing knowledge)

- **Confirm only the FIRST coordinate guess with a screenshot; after that, trust the resulting state change or escalate to relaunch — don't screenshot-confirm every single tap.** Screenshot-confirming each guess doubles the cost per attempt (tap → screenshot → OCR → re-screenshot). First-guess confirm only; then trust the state change (or apply R-NEW-1). *Evidence: QA Task 15 P4 — each guessed tap on the stuck alert was re-screenshot + re-OCR'd, doubling the ~20-call cost.*
- **Dedupe guards mean a "fresh" fixture may not actually be fresh.** A review/trade left over from a prior session can block the intended path (e.g., "You have already reported this review"). Check DB state before assuming a clean path, and pivot to an alternate fixture (e.g., a second persona's review) rather than re-driving the blocked one. *Evidence: QA Task 15 A2 (Q15 — target review already reported from QA Task 14; pivoted to Anonymous User's review `20c09442`); F10 (two identical "QA Canned Cancelled-Trade Item" trades — refunded vs non-refunded).*
- **The disclaimer modal requires checking the "I have read and understand" checkbox before "Accept and continue" becomes active — do the checkbox first.** The first tap on Accept does nothing until the checkbox is checked (correct gating, but undiscovered). Confirms §5.42 R30's `disclaimer-modal-checkbox` geometry/flow as the standing path; add the checkbox-first step to any bundle/offer accept flow. *Evidence: QA Task 15 C3 — ~4 calls spent rediscovering the gate (F8).*

### 5.48 Standing rules — QA Task 16 friction-analysis fixes (2026-09-01) — R-16-1..5 (zero dev cost)

Zero-dev-cost rules derived from the QA Task 16 decision-and-outcome log — evidence source: `e2e-test-results/qa-task16-close-trd-2026-08-31/decision-outcome-log.md` (18 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 BLOCKED; friction dropped to ~38 of ~150–170 calls vs QA Task 15's ~90 — R-NEW-1..6 + DT76/DT77 instrumentation worked as intended). The remaining frictions are small; the two biggest (F1 in-progress-bundle cancel ~11 calls, F2 MAX_PENDING_OFFERS reset ~13 calls) are a product decision + a missed standing rule, both removable with zero QA tooling. All five rules are **pure playbook/memory discipline — no dev work required — and apply from the very next QA session.** They sit alongside R-NEW-1..6 (§5.47) and the R1–R41 sequence. Companion dated consolidation in `/memories/repo/qa-test-agent.md` (2026-09-01 entry).

**R-16-1 — Reset offer/cart fixtures FIRST, always.** Before any session that touches offers, bundles, or carts, run `npm run qa:reset-offer-fixtures` as the very first action — before assembling any fixture — and note the pre-state. This run hit `MAX_PENDING_OFFERS` mid-session and paid ~13 calls for a reset-and-rebuild (ef-repro → dry-run reset → live reset → cart rebuild → re-submit) that a single call up front would have avoided entirely. Strengthens R26 (§5.43): R26 verifies fixtures before assembling; R-16-1 makes the reset the standing first action of any offer/bundle session. *Evidence: QA Task 16 A1 — HTTP 409 `MAX_PENDING_OFFERS` on the Kids Bicycle resubmit after the T06 bundle left 3 pending slots with test-seller (F2).*

**R-16-2 — In-progress bundle trades have NO app-side cancel; go straight to admin.** Confirmed in source: the bundle Trade Timeline exposes no cancel control (only Request Extension / Confirm / Report Problem) — cancel exists only on the single-trade TradeDetailScreen, unreachable from a bundle view. To free an in-progress bundle fixture, go directly to the admin "Force Cancel Entire Bundle" mechanism (the W10 mechanism). Do NOT attempt the app UI first — it is a confirmed dead end that cost ~11 calls to discover. Note: `p2pkidsmarketplace://trade/<id>` NOW works (DT77) and is no longer a dead end per R-NEW-2's cache — but for in_progress bundle trades it lands on the bundle Trade Timeline, which still has no cancel. *Evidence: QA Task 16 A1 — Kids Bicycle locked in leftover in-progress bundle `5b69480b`; freed via admin force-cancel (F1).*

**R-16-3 — Category-level SP caps are written via the admin portal only.** `categories.sp_redemption_cap` is set via the admin portal's `/categories` → Edit → SP Config tab — NOT via `qa:admin-config-set` (R37, §5.44), which only covers the `admin_config` table. When a case touches a category SP cap, use the scope-write-then-revert-verify discipline (R28): set the cap, verify the mobile hint + server reject, then revert and DB-verify the column is back to its prior state. *Evidence: QA Task 16 A4 — Sports `sp_redemption_cap=5` → "Accepts Points · Up to 5 SP" + `qa:ef-repro` with `sp_amount:10` → HTTP 400 `SP_CAP_EXCEEDED`; reverted to NULL (F3, 12 calls).*

**R-16-4 — Prefer ONE bounded functional tap over a color-scan loop for disabled-state assertions.** When a control's disabled state is not exposed in the AX tree (no `accessibilityState.disabled`), do exactly ONE functional tap to confirm the no-op, then move on — never loop with repeated color-scans or re-screenshots. **FIX-DISABLED landed in DEV-TASK-79 (2026-09-01):** `disclaimer-modal-accept-button` carries `accessibilityState={{disabled}}` (present since TASK SAFETY-008, unit-tested) plus a new `accessibilityHint` that states the gating — so FIRST re-list the AX tree and look for `disabled:true` / the hint on `disclaimer-modal-accept-button`; if it still isn't surfaced, relaunch the app once (R-NEW-1 — a stale JS bundle hides newly-instrumented elements) before falling back to the single functional tap. *Evidence: QA Task 16 I06 — the disclaimer accept-button gate was proven with a functional tap (unchecked → tap Accept → modal stays open) because the AX tree did not surface `accessibilityState.disabled` (F4, ~3 calls).*

**R-16-5 — Read a deep link's ACTUAL param names before firing it with crafted values.** Don't guess deep-link parameter names from intuition (e.g., assuming `spUsed` drives a dollar figure when the actual param is `spAmountDollars`). Check the handler's source (`QaForceTradeSuccessDeepLinkHandler.tsx` or the target screen's route-param reads) or existing memory notes first — one wrong guess costs a wasted round-trip. *Evidence: QA Task 16 H02 — "You saved $8 using SP!" rendered as "You saved $0.00" on the first `qa-trade-success` attempt because the dollar figure is driven by `spAmountDollars`, not `spUsed` (F6, ~2 calls).*

### 5.49 Standing rule — `run_playwright_code` deferred-result (2-call) pattern (DEV-TASK-79, 2026-09-01) — R-16-6 (expected behavior, not friction)

The admin-portal browser driver (`run_playwright_code`) returns a **`deferredResultId`** for mutating/state-changing scripts — the script keeps running in the background and the tool returns immediately with an ID; the result must be fetched with a **second call** that passes that `deferredResultId` (resuming the deferred execution). This is the TOOL'S DESIGNED contract for mutations that outlive the inline window (the F5 friction from QA Task 16, and F3 from QA Task 15) — NOT a defect, and NOT friction to rediscover each run. Standing expectations:

- **Expect the 2-call pattern on every mutating admin script:** call 1 returns `deferredResultId`; call 2 passes it straight back and returns the script's final output/verdict. Never retry the whole script when you get a `deferredResultId` — resume it.
- **Read-only scripts usually return inline** (no `deferredResultId`); only mutations defer.
- **Batch to pay the tax once per page interaction, not once per action (extends R-NEW-5):** drive each admin page interaction as ONE script that clicks, reads the resulting state, and returns a compact JSON verdict. One batched script = one deferred round-trip; N per-action scripts = N deferred round-trips.
- **Return inline JSON verdicts, never raw snapshots:** have the script itself return `{status, asserted, observed}` (or similar) so the second call's output is directly verdict-ready and no 76KB-snapshot + grep follows.
- **Budget calls with the tax in mind:** count a mutating admin interaction as 2 calls (script + deferred fetch), a read-only one as 1.
- **Companion app-side instrumentation (DEV-TASK-79):** where an admin/QA script must assert an app element's AX-exposed state, prefer the now-identifiable elements over OCR/color-scan — `includes-points-redemption-tag` on both bundle-card variants (FIX-AX) and `disclaimer-modal-accept-button`'s `accessibilityState.disabled` + `accessibilityHint` (FIX-DISABLED).

*Evidence: QA Task 15 F3 (~40+ calls for 12 admin cases, mostly per-action 2-call deferred executions + snapshot greps) and QA Task 16 F5 (admin `run_playwright_code` deferred 2-call tax, ~6 calls/run).*

### 5.50 Standing rule — Driving Stripe hosted Checkout in browser legs (QA Task 21, 2026-09-02) — expected friction, not app defects

When a case requires completing or declining a real **Stripe hosted Checkout** (web-first subscription purchase / decline-card path), the Stripe page has documented, repeatable behaviors that are NOT app defects — drive them directly:

- **Link interstitials:** Stripe interjects a "Confirm it's you" / Link fast-checkout step (it remembers a returning email). Click **"Pay without Link"** (`button:has-text("Pay without Link")`) to reach the raw card form. If a 6-digit "code sent to (•••) ••• ••34" step appears in test mode, the page itself states "You are currently testing and no code will be sent. Enter 000000 to continue."
- **Required phone field:** hosted Checkout collects a phone number (placeholder "(201) 555-0123") before Subscribe is accepted — fill a valid test number (`input[placeholder="(201) 555-0123"]`).
- **Card fields live in the MAIN checkout frame** after selecting the **Card** radio (`#payment-method-accordion-item-title-card`); the card-number field uses placeholder "1234 1234 1234 1234". Fill via `input[placeholder=...]` in Playwright (scan main frame + subframes; the fields appear in the main frame).
- **`page.screenshot` on Stripe pages can time out waiting for fonts** even with `animations: 'disabled'` — prefer DOM-text evidence (the red `FieldError` element, `inputValue()` read-backs) + the embedded screenshot OCR for decline/error assertions.
- **Decline test card 4000 0000 0000 0002** → red `FieldError` "Your card was declined. Please try a different card."; assert no subscription/billing row was created and no partial state was left (an abandoned Checkout creates an empty customer — a cleanup candidate).
- **No-profile emails:** the web `/api/checkout` → `create-checkout-session` EF issues a bind token for emails with no app profile; if `SUBSCRIPTION_BIND_TOKEN_SECRET` is unset on staging it returns 500 "Key length is zero" — for decline/success Checkout legs prefer a profile-backed email (e.g. test-free) so the session resolves by `client_reference_id`.

*Evidence: QA Task 21 Sections A/B — every real Checkout needed 1–3 extra round-trips for Link + phone before the decline/success assertion could run.*

### 5.51 Standing rules — MSG first-live round efficiency (QA Test Agent Efficiency Playbook v1, 2026-09-03) — R42–R49 + forward-looking instrumentation

Zero-dev-cost rules derived from the MSG manual-testing guide's first live round — evidence source: `e2e-test-results/qa-msg-first-live-2026-09-03/decision-outcome-log.md` (+ `report.md`; 23 PASS / 0 FAIL / 1 BLOCKED (B05 screen-render, fixture-gated after a real reachability finding) / 1 NOT-SUPPORTED (J05); ~235–250 calls, of which ~30–40% is projected reducible by the rules below + the pending instrumentation in §5.51b). All eight rules are **pure playbook/memory discipline — no dev work required — and apply from the very next QA session.** They sit alongside R-16-1..6 (§5.48/§5.49), R-NEW-1..6 (§5.47), and the R1–R41 sequence. Where a rule restates an existing §5.x/§6.x section (R19/§5.26 batch-by-persona, §5.33 repurpose incidental state, the §5.47b dedupe-guards codified fact, §6.1 two-source corroboration, R-NEW-2 deep-link navigation), the earlier section remains canonical and this entry adds the sharper trigger + the measured evidence + the cheaper response. Companion dated consolidation in `/memories/repo/qa-test-agent.md` (2026-09-03 entry).

**R42 — Deep-link-first, but verify the linking config BEFORE firing.** Before trusting any guide's "reachable via `/x` deep link" claim, grep `AppNavigator`'s `linking.config.screens` for that path FIRST. Only fire the deep link and investigate after failure if the source check is inconclusive. Sharpens R-NEW-2 (§5.47 — deep-link-first + a cached dead-end list) and §5.25 (fail fast from source): R-NEW-2 says navigate-by-deep-link and cache dead ends; R42 says verify the path is even REGISTERED in `linking.config.screens` before the first `openurl` — this turns the run's ~9-call dead-end discovery into a ~30-second check. Keep the cache current because the config changes over time (DT77 registered TradeDetail/TradeTimeline, so `/trade/<id>` went from dead end to working — R-16-2's note is the model). *Evidence: MSG P1 B05 — `/leaderboard` fired twice → no navigation; a 30-second grep showed `linking.config.screens` has NO `Leaderboard` path (nor `Badges`/`SpWallet`/`Referrals`/`Chat`/`TradeList`) and `deepLink.ts` is only the notification deep-link service, so a raw `/leaderboard` can never navigate — provable BEFORE firing. On this build `/trade/<id>` and `/seller-profile/<userId>` ARE registered and confirmed working (use them as primary entries); `/leaderboard` is not (its only real entry is a `leaderboard_rank_up` notification tap, and no such notification exists for any user → B05's render leg is BLOCKED, not a retry).*

**R43 — DB dedupe/pre-condition check before shared-data mutations.** On any shared (non-disposable) persona, run a quick read-only query for existing state that would dead-end the intended action ("already reported", "already reviewed", an existing pending offer, etc.) BEFORE attempting it in the UI. Sharpens the §5.47b dedupe-guards codified fact (check DB before assuming a "fresh" path) and R-NEW-6 (§5.47 fixture-feasibility) into a standing pre-mutation gate for the shared-data-mutation class. *Evidence: MSG P4 C06 — the `review_reports` pre-check showed `20c09442` + `14372222` were already reported by test-seller from prior QA; ONE query picked the clean target (`8b65662d`, Test Buyer's 4★) and killed a guaranteed "already reported" dead-end in a single call.*

**R44 — On pinned-header scrollables, tap only mid-viewport controls.** Never tap a scroll-list toggle/button whose AX-logical y-coordinate could fall inside a pinned header's tap band. The AX tree reports scroll-content coordinates that RENDER UNDER a fixed header, so a tap at that logical y hits the header's control instead (a real mis-tap that opened the wrong screen this run). Rule: on any scrollable screen with a pinned header, only tap controls sitting mid-viewport (well below the header's bottom edge); if a target reports inside the header band, scroll it down first and re-list. Complements R22 (§5.40 viewport/occlusion pre-tap gate) and R31 (§5.42 tab-bar occlusion) — the pinned-header band is a THIRD occlusion source the tree does not flag. *Evidence: MSG P2/P3 — tapping `toggle-trades-push` at its AX-logical y94 hit the fixed header bell (`header-notifications-btn` occupies the same band) → opened Notification Center → the detour + J01 re-do + diagnosis cost ~6 calls. Tooling fix pending: `qa:ax-tree` header-band occlusion flag (§5.51b).*

**R45 — A fully AX-exposed screen: read it in ONE tree parse.** When a screen is fully AX-exposed, do ONE full tree parse to enumerate categories, toggles, counts, and footer copy instead of issuing multiple small list/tap calls. One parse answers most assertions at once — this run's cheapest phases were exactly the ones done this way. Where the inline tree output truncates, the FULL tree is written to the session-resource file — grep that file rather than issuing more list calls. *Evidence: MSG P3 Group J (5 categories + per-category toggles + Quiet Hours + footer copy resolved from ~1–2 parses) and P6 Referrals (hero/code/rewards/history asserted from a single parse).*

**R46 — Source-read the exact visual rule before pixel work.** Before any pixel-scan or OCR pass, read the component source for the EXACT color/state logic so the on-device check is one targeted confirmation, not an exploratory scan. Complements §6.1's evidence discipline and R18 (§5.39 source-pre-read) for the visual/pixel layer specifically: source tells you the precise rule (a hex, a disabled/conditional state, an `INITIAL_VISIBLE` constant), so one region-scoped scan or OCR suffices. *Evidence: MSG P1 B01/B02 — source read gave earned-cell `#FFF9EC` vs locked `#F7F7F7`@0.6 + `#999999` label → one targeted `qa:badge-scan` region confirmed 40.4% cream → PASS; MSG P5 A08 — `QuickReplyChips.tsx`'s `INITIAL_VISIBLE=3` made the on-device "3 chips + More" check a confirmation, not exploration.*

**R47 — Two-source corroboration for unobservable UI states (empty states, DB-gated renders).** For anything a screenshot cannot directly prove — empty states, subtle copy nuances, DB-gated renders — corroborate from TWO independent sources: the source/render-condition code AND the DB/data path (§6.1's two-source rule), rather than reporting "unverified" or trusting an unobservable UI. Extends §6.1's Phase-23 two-source corroboration to the empty-state and DB-gated classes (and covers the case where the UI shows nothing because a fixture row doesn't exist). *Evidence: MSG P1 B03 — after scroll overshoot hid the badge showcase strip, the strip assertion rested on source (names present) + OCR of an earlier frame rather than a re-drive; MSG P1 B05 — the render leg was BLOCKED with evidence because the DB query returned ZERO `leaderboard_rank_up` notifications for any user (the only real entry to Leaderboard).*

**R48 — Reuse incidental navigation states — extend to whole-group execution.** If an accidental tap lands somewhere with useful fixture state, consider running that area's cases IN PLACE instead of navigating back and discarding the state. Extends §5.33 (repurpose incidental state) from single-interaction recovery to whole-group execution: an incidental destination can be a ready-made fixture for a whole sub-group. *Evidence: MSG P2 — the P3 header mis-tap opened Notification Center with 25+ unread rows for test-buyer, which is exactly Group I's fixture, so I03–I05 ran in-place (net-neutral detour) instead of navigating away and losing the state.*

**R49 — Batch all cases needing the same persona together BEFORE switching.** Each persona switch carries a standing "login tax" (~3 calls: logout / `qa-login-as` openurl / tree-poll verify, plus re-navigation on arrival) that compounds when interleaved. Reaffirms R19 (§5.39) and §5.26 (batch by persona) with a quantified tax so run plans order work persona-major, not guide-major. *Evidence: MSG P4 — 2 persona switches (buyer→seller for C05/C06, seller→buyer for C01–C04) cost ~6 calls; ordering by persona would have removed the extra round-trip.*

### 5.51b Forward-looking instrumentation (pending dev task — NOT yet behavioral rules)

The following permanent tooling/app-side fixes are queued as a separate dev task and will REMOVE most of the manual workarounds in R42–R49. Until they land, the manual rules above are the documented path; once they land, **update the affected rules to reflect the new tooling capability** (e.g., turn a per-tile scan into a one-read tree assertion) rather than leaving the manual workaround as the only documented path:

- **Per-tile AX labels/testIDs on image grids and icon chips** (My Badges grid tiles, notification icon chips, badge-detail-modal Close) — turns the R46/R45 pixel+OCR work into one-read tree assertions (BP-53). Applies to B01/B02/B03 and I03 grid/icon assertions.
- **`qa:ax-tree` header-band occlusion flag** — flag any element whose logical y overlaps a pinned header's band, catching the R44 trap before a tap.
- **`qa:scroll-to?testID=` helper** (deep link or tool) — returns fresh mid-viewport coordinates in one call, removing the flingy-scroll positioning cost behind R44/R49-adjacent scrolling (Profile showcase, long lists).
- **AX-visible `keyboard-done-button` on multiline TextInputs** (e.g. the review comment field) — one-tap in-app keyboard dismiss instead of the Cmd+K round-trip.
- **1–2 new deep links:** register the missing paths in `AppNavigator.linking.config.screens` (`Leaderboard`, `Badges`, `SpWallet`, `Referrals`, `Chat`, `TradeList` — unblocks R42-class reachability claims and corrects the B05 guide finding) and add `/submit-review?tradeId=` to remove the My Trades → timeline → scroll → Review-button hop (~6 calls/case).
- **`leaderboard_rank_up` fixture or `qa-badge-award` trigger** for a test persona — unblocks B05's render leg AND B04's celebration modal (currently nothing can reach Leaderboard live).
- **Schema cheat-sheet update** — fold the verified MSG table column sets into `/memories/repo/schema-cheat-sheet.md` so P0 recon is one query instead of guess-and-verify (R-NEW-3 standing duty).

### 5.52 Standing rule — QA Task 24 (MSG-complete) load-time persistence (2026-09-03) — R50

Zero-dev-cost discipline derived from the QA Task 24 MSG-completion run — evidence source: `e2e-test-results/qa-task24-msg-complete-2026-09-03/report.md` + `ledger.md`. This rule closes the gap where §5.7 defines the load-time measurement but nothing required the measurements to survive to handoff time.

**R50 — Persist every §5.7 load-time measurement into the run's notes/report AT CAPTURE TIME, not in working memory.** A run is not complete until the §8.2 batch load-time table and the §8.3 Perceived Load-Time Verdict are populated from recorded measurements — never reconstructed from memory at the end of the run. When a timed transition (§5.7) is measured, immediately write its row (screen → transition → start/end → elapsed time, labeled per §5.7) into the run's report/notes — maintain a running per-transition table continuously in-session so no measurement is lost between capture and handoff and the Perceived Load-Time Verdict is never left thin or stated from general impression alone. Extends §5.7 (which defines the measurement + the ≥3s flag rule) with a persistence/completeness requirement; it is the load-time analog of R16 (§5.39 — keep a running friction/facts list in session memory throughout the run), applied to timed-transition data. *Evidence: QA Task 24 — systematic per-transition stopwatch data was not retained during the run, so the §8.3 Perceived Load-Time Verdict could only be stated as GOOD from general observation instead of from a populated §8.2 table; that gap was flagged in the run's own "Suggested to improve agent rules" entry.*

### 5.53 Standing rule — QA Task 25 consolidated-round efficiency (2026-09-03) — R51

Zero-dev-cost rule from the QA Task 25 consolidated round — evidence source: `e2e-test-results/qa-task25-consolidated-2026-09-03/report.md` + `ledger.md`. Where it restates an existing section (R42/§5.51 deep-link-first + verify the linking config, R-NEW-2/§5.47 deep-link-first navigation, §5.9 small-swipe discipline), the earlier section remains canonical and this entry adds the sharper trigger + the measured evidence + the cheaper response.

**R51 — On long scrollables, treat the Profile ScrollView as flingy and prefer the target screen's REGISTERED deep link over swipe-and-relist navigation.** The Profile ScrollView (like Home) moves ~950pt per swipe **regardless of the requested distance** (flingy), so swipe-and-relist navigation to a below-fold Profile menu row repeatedly overshoots the target (this session: Billing History and the ID-verification row each cost repeated overshoot/list cycles before a deep link was used). When a case's next destination is a Profile sub-screen, fire its deep link instead — verify it is registered in `AppNavigator.linking.config.screens` first (per R42), then `xcrun simctl openurl`. Confirmed-working Profile sub-screen deep links on the current build: `billing-history` → Transaction History, `id-verification-upload` → ID Verification upload, `manage-kids-club` → Manage Kids Club+, `referrals`, `badges`, `sp-wallet`, `trades`, `listing-safety/:listing_id`. Only fall back to scrolling when the target row has no registered deep link — and then use screenshot-OCR positioning or small controlled swipes (§5.9) rather than blind swipe-and-relist. Updates R-NEW-2's running deep-link cache with the working Profile sub-screen entries. *Evidence: QA Task 25 — Profile-menu targets (Billing History at `profile-billing-history`, ID Verification at `id-verification-menu-item`) required repeated flingy-scroll overshoots (~950pt/gesture) before the deep links (`billing-history`, `id-verification-upload`) reached the same screens in one call.*

### 5.54 Standing rule — per-case status tracker `QA-TESTCASE-STATUS-2026-09-03.md` is the source of truth and MUST be updated every QA round (R52, 2026-09-03)

The file **`e2e-test-results/QA-TESTCASE-STATUS-2026-09-03.md`** is the **canonical per-case status tracker** for every test case in the 6 consolidated guides under `cross-checked-and-consolidated/` (833 canonical TC-IDs: AUTH 138 · MSG 72 · TRD 288 · ACC 75 · ADM 160 · SUB 100). For day-to-day per-case status it **supersedes the older `TEST-COVERAGE-INVENTORY.md` reference in R8** — R8's "trust the tracker over inline guide annotations" now means trust THIS file (and the underlying reconciliation in `TEST-COVERAGE-INVENTORY-v2.md` / `temp/tc-inventory-v2/`). A guide's inline "passed" stamp is only trustworthy when this tracker shows a verdict for that TC-ID.

**R52 — After EVERY QA round (per batch §8.2 AND at session close, BEFORE emitting the §8.3 QA Session Handoff), update the tracker with this round's results.** A round is not complete until the tracker is updated and the §8.3 `Coverage Tracker Updated` field is filled.

1. **Which rows to touch.** For every TC-ID this round produced or refreshed a verdict, update that row in its guide's "Completed test cases" table — `Status` (✅ PASS / 🟡 PARTIAL / 🔴 STILL OPEN / 📄 DOC-DRIFT / ⏭️ SKIPPED), `Latest`, `Date`, `Source`, `Notes`. Set `Source` to this run's folder (e.g. `e2e-test-results/<run>/report.md`) and `Date` to the run date. **Move any TC now covered out of that guide's "Remaining test cases — NEVER RUN" list.** If a case that previously PASSed is FAIL/BLOCKED this round, mark it 🔴 STILL OPEN with the reason — never silently keep the stale PASS.
2. **Refresh the roll-ups.** Update the §1 per-guide roll-up table counts (PASS / PARTIAL / OPEN / DRIFT / SKIPPED / Remaining) to match the edited rows.
3. **When to do it.** Update the tracker continuously after each batch within a multi-batch session (analogous to R50/R16 persistence), and do a final reconciliation pass at session close so the file always reflects the latest state before handoff. Do not defer the update to "the next consolidation round."
4. **This is a permitted deliverable-surface write.** The tracker lives under `e2e-test-results/`, the agent's approved evidence/deliverable archive per §5.14 — updating it (via file-edit tools, never shell redirection) is the same class of write as producing `report.md`. No code/guide/report files are modified; updating the tracker is execution-output documentation.
5. **Regeneration consistency.** The tracker is generated from the reconciliation data in `temp/tc-inventory-v2/` (curated TRD map + auto-reconciled rows; `build_status_tracker.py`). Because TRD verdicts are curated from the run reports, always ALSO record this round's per-TC verdicts in the run's `report.md`/`ledger.md` so a later regeneration reproduces what you wrote in the tracker. If the tracker is ever regenerated from the data layer, your in-place edits must already be represented there.
6. **Handoff integration.** The §8.3 QA Session Handoff block carries a required `Coverage Tracker Updated` field (list every TC-ID flipped from Remaining → Completed, or whose Latest/Status changed, plus the new per-guide totals). Per §8.4 that field also appears in the agent's final chat-visible reply. A run that does not update the tracker must state that as an explicit exception with a reason.

*Evidence: `e2e-test-results/QA-TESTCASE-STATUS-2026-09-03.md` and `TEST-COVERAGE-INVENTORY-v2.md` created 2026-09-03 (no-cutoff reconciliation of all QA evidence on disk; supersedes the 2026-08-24 inventory that omitted TRD Groups S–Z, ACC closures, and the MSG/SUB live rounds).*

### 5.55 Standing rule — the FORMAL QA Session Handoff (complete §8.3 block, every field) is the MANDATORY final-chat deliverable of every QA run (R53, 2026-09-04)

**R53 — Every QA run MUST end with the complete formal QA Session Handoff — the full §8.3 block with EVERY field populated — emitted verbatim as part of the agent's FINAL chat-visible reply. A condensed summary, a "see the report" pointer, a partial field set, or prose that paraphrases the fields is NOT acceptable and does not complete the run.** This is a hard, non-negotiable contract between the QA agent and the humans (project owner / dev agent) who consume the agent's output — the formal handoff block is the *only* reliably-scanned status artifact the humans read, so it must be complete and self-contained in the chat message every single time.

1. **Trigger.** The rule applies to the END of EVERY run — every per-case report (§8.1), every batch summary (§8.2), and every multi-case session close — regardless of run size (one case or one hundred), verdict mix (all-PASS or all-BLOCKED), or surface (mobile-only, admin-only, or mixed). It is not optional and is not skippable on "small run" or "nothing to report" grounds — a run with zero findings still emits the block with explicit "None" / "not applicable" values.
2. **What "every field" means.** Reproduce the §8.3 block's field set exactly and verbatim (field labels intact), and fill every field with real content from this run — do not delete or merge fields:
   - `**Test Scope:**`
   - `**Design-System Compliance:**`
   - `**Perceived Load-Time Verdict:**`
   - `**Design & Copy Compliance Confirmation:**`
   - `**Verdict Summary:**`
   - `**Coverage Tracker Updated:**`
   - `**Critical Findings:**`
   - `**App State Left Behind:**`
   - `**Why It Matters:**`
   - `**How to Verify/Reproduce:**`
   - `**Known Gaps / Not Tested:**`
   - `**What Needs To Be Fixed Next:**`
   - `**UX Enhancement Ideas (optional, not defects):**`
   - `**Suggested Next Session:**`
   - `**Suggested to Improve Agent Rules:**`
   Where a field has no content this run, write the explicit null phrase required by the template (e.g. "None — all reachable behavior in this batch is correct.", "None this run — no friction or enhancement opportunities observed…", "none") — never leave the field blank and never omit the label.
3. **No "file-only" escape, and no summary substitute.** §8.4 already forbids file-only emission; R53 additionally forbids replacing the verbatim block with a condensed bullet list, a "top-line verdict + see report.md" hand-wave, or a link. The detailed per-case traces/screenshots/tables stay in `report.md`; the *complete handoff block itself* is repeated verbatim in the final chat reply.
